source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired diversity of earlier revelation and ancestral audience.
verses.before: Long ago, at many times and in many ways, God spoke to our fathers by the prophets,
verses.after: Long ago, God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets in many portions and in many ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: Long ago, at many times and in many ways, God spoke to our fathers by the prophets,

verses.rationale: Keeps the anarthrous Son expression, inheritance and creation of the ages.
verses.before: but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of everything, through whom also he made the ages.
verses.after: In these last days, he has spoken to us through a Son, whom he appointed heir of all things and through whom he also made the ages.
verses.tsw_comparator: but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the ages.

verses.rationale: Preserves radiance/imprint images, cosmic sustaining and enthronement after purification.
verses.before: He is the radiance of the glory of God and the exact imprint of his being, and he upholds everything by the word of his power. After making purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
verses.after: The Son is the radiance of God's glory and the exact imprint of his being, sustaining all things by his powerful word. After making purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.
verses.tsw_comparator: He is the radiance of the glory of God and the exact imprint of his being, and he upholds all things by the word of his power. After making purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,

verses.rationale: Keeps comparative logic and inherited name unnamed.
verses.before: having become as much superior to the angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs.
verses.after: He became as much superior to the angels as the name he inherited is more excellent than theirs.
verses.tsw_comparator: having become as much superior to the angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs.

verses.rationale: Retains rhetorical question and both kinship quotations.
verses.before: For to which of the angels did God ever say, “You are my Son, today I have begotten you”? Or again, “I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son”?
verses.after: For to which of the angels did God ever say, “You are my Son; today I have fathered you”? Or again, “I will be his Father, and he will be my Son”?
verses.tsw_comparator: For to which of the angels did God ever say, “You are my Son, today I have begotten you”? Or again, “I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son”?

verses.rationale: Keeps firstborn title, world entrance and angelic worship.
verses.before: And again, when he brings the firstborn into the world, he says, “Let all God’s angels worship him.”
verses.after: And again, when he brings the firstborn into the inhabited world, he says, “Let all God's angels worship him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And again, when he brings the firstborn into the world, he says, “Let all God’s angels worship him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves wind/spirit ambiguity as winds and the fire image.
verses.before: Of the angels he says, “He makes his angels winds, and his ministers a flame of fire.”
verses.after: About the angels he says, “He makes his angels winds, and his servants flames of fire.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Of the angels he says, “He makes his angels winds, and his ministers a flame of fire.”

verses.rationale: Keeps direct divine address and rule imagery.
verses.before: But of the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom.
verses.after: But about the Son: “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, and the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: But of the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom.

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled God language, anointing and comparison.
verses.before: You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions.”
verses.after: You loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, your God, anointed you with the oil of joy beyond your companions.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness beyond your companions.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Lord address, foundation and handwork imagery.
verses.before: And, “You, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the work of your hands;
verses.after: And, “In the beginning, Lord, you laid the earth's foundation, and the heavens are the works of your hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: And, “You, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the work of your hands;

verses.rationale: Retains creation's impermanence and garment simile.
verses.before: they will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like a garment,
verses.after: They will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like clothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: they will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like a garment,

verses.rationale: Keeps rolling/changing imagery and divine constancy.
verses.before: like a robe you will roll them up, like a garment they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will have no end.”
verses.after: You will roll them up like a cloak; like clothing they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will never end.”
verses.tsw_comparator: like a robe you will roll them up, like a garment they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will have no end.”

verses.rationale: Preserves enthronement, enemies and subjugating footstool image.
verses.before: And to which of the angels has he ever said, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet”?
verses.after: And to which of the angels has he ever said, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet”?
verses.tsw_comparator: And to which of the angels has he ever said, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet”?

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical form, angelic service and future inheritance.
verses.before: Are they not all ministering spirits sent out to serve for the sake of people who are to inherit salvation?
verses.after: Are they not all serving spirits sent out to minister for the sake of those who are about to inherit salvation?
verses.tsw_comparator: Are they not all ministering spirits sent out to serve for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation?

verses.rationale: Retains heightened attention and drifting image.
verses.before: So we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, lest we drift away from it.
verses.after: Therefore, we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, lest we drift away from it.

verses.rationale: Keeps angelic mediation, legal violations and deserved recompense.
verses.before: For since the message declared through angels proved reliable, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense,
verses.after: For if the message spoken through angels proved reliable, and every transgression and disobedience received just repayment,
verses.tsw_comparator: For since the message declared through angels proved reliable, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense,

verses.rationale: Preserves rhetorical warning and the transmission sequence.
verses.before: how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It was declared at first by the Lord, and it was attested to us by people who heard,
verses.after: how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It was first spoken through the Lord and confirmed to us by those who heard him,
verses.tsw_comparator: how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It was declared at first by the Lord, and it was attested to us by those who heard,

verses.rationale: Keeps all four divine attestations and sovereign distribution.
verses.before: while God also bore witness by signs and wonders and various miracles and by gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to his will.
verses.after: while God also testified with signs, wonders, various miracles and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to his will.
verses.tsw_comparator: while God also bore witness by signs and wonders and various miracles and by gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to his will.

verses.rationale: Retains future world and denial of angelic rule.
verses.before: For it was not to angels that God subjected the world to come, of which we are speaking.
verses.after: For it was not to angels that he subjected the coming inhabited world, about which we are speaking.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it was not to angels that God subjected the world to come, of which we are speaking.

verses.rationale: Keeps the author's indefinite citation formula and gendered representative human.
verses.before: It has been testified somewhere, “What is man, that you are mindful of him, or the son of man, that you care for him?
verses.after: But someone has testified somewhere: “What is a human being that you remember him, or a son of man that you care for him?
verses.tsw_comparator: It has been testified somewhere, “What is man, that you are mindful of him, or the son of man, that you care for him?

verses.rationale: Preserves temporal/spatial ambiguity of little and crowning.
verses.before: You made him for a little while lower than the angels; you have crowned him with glory and honor,
verses.after: You made him lower than the angels for a little while; you crowned him with glory and honor
verses.tsw_comparator: You made him for a little while lower than the angels; you have crowned him with glory and honor,

verses.rationale: Keeps universal subjection and the present empirical tension.
verses.before: putting everything in subjection under his feet.” Now in putting everything in subjection to him, he left nothing outside his control. At present, we do not yet see everything in subjection to him.
verses.after: and subjected everything beneath his feet.” By subjecting everything to him, God left nothing outside his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subjected to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: putting everything in subjection under his feet.” Now in putting everything in subjection to him, he left nothing outside his control. At present, we do not yet see everything in subjection to him.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned ‘apart from God’ reading rather than silently substituting ‘by grace.’
verses.before: But we see him who for a little while was made lower than the angels, namely Jesus, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.
verses.after: But we see Jesus, made lower than the angels for a little while, crowned with glory and honor because he suffered death, so that apart from God he might taste death for everyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: But we see him who for a little while was made lower than the angels, namely Jesus, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine purpose, filial image, pioneer title and suffering.
verses.before: For it was fitting that he, for whom and by whom everything exist, in bringing many sons to glory, should make the founder of their salvation perfect through suffering.
verses.after: For it was fitting that God, for whom and through whom all things exist, in bringing many sons and daughters to glory, should perfect the pioneer of their salvation through sufferings.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it was fitting that he, for whom and by whom all things exist, in bringing many sons to glory, should make the founder of their salvation perfect through suffering.

verses.rationale: Preserves shared origin and family naming.
verses.before: For he who sanctifies and people who are sanctified all have one source. That is why he is not ashamed to call them brothers and sisters,
verses.after: For the one who makes holy and those being made holy all come from one. That is why he is not ashamed to call them brothers and sisters,
verses.tsw_comparator: For he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified all have one source. That is why he is not ashamed to call them brothers,

verses.rationale: Keeps public proclamation and congregational song.
verses.before: saying, “I will tell of your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will sing your praise.”
verses.after: saying, “I will proclaim your name to my brothers and sisters; in the midst of the assembly I will sing your praise.”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “I will tell of your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will sing your praise.”

verses.rationale: Retains both quotations and child imagery.
verses.before: And again, “I will put my trust in him.” And again, “Behold, I and the children God has given me.”
verses.after: And again, “I will put my trust in him.” And again, “Here I am, with the children God gave me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And again, “I will put my trust in him.” And again, “Behold, I and the children God has given me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps human embodiment, death as means and named opponent.
verses.before: Since therefore the children share in flesh and blood, he himself likewise shared in the same things, that through death he might destroy the one who has the power of death, that is, the devil,
verses.after: Since the children share in blood and flesh, he too shared in the same things, so that through death he might render powerless the one who holds the power of death—that is, the devil—
verses.tsw_comparator: Since therefore the children share in flesh and blood, he himself likewise shared in the same things, that through death he might destroy the one who has the power of death, that is, the devil,

verses.rationale: Preserves lifelong fear and slavery language.
verses.before: and deliver all people who through fear of death were subject to lifelong slavery.
verses.after: and free those who were held in slavery all their lives by fear of death.
verses.tsw_comparator: and deliver all those who through fear of death were subject to lifelong slavery.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated grasping and Abrahamic lineage.
verses.before: For surely it is not angels that he helps, but he helps the offspring of Abraham.
verses.after: For clearly he does not take hold of angels, but he takes hold of Abraham's offspring.
verses.tsw_comparator: For surely it is not angels that he helps, but he helps the offspring of Abraham.

verses.rationale: Retains necessity, full likeness and priestly atonement.
verses.before: So he had to be made like his brothers and sisters in every respect, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the service of God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
verses.after: Therefore, he had to become like his brothers and sisters in every way, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in matters relating to God, to make atonement for the people's sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore he had to be made like his brothers in every respect, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the service of God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.

verses.rationale: Keeps suffering, testing and aid grounded in experience.
verses.before: For because he himself has suffered when tempted, he can help people who are being tempted.
verses.after: Because he himself suffered when tested, he is able to help those being tested.
verses.tsw_comparator: For because he himself has suffered when tempted, he is able to help those who are being tempted.

verses.rationale: Preserves communal titles and both unusual roles of Jesus.
verses.before: So, holy brothers and sisters, sharers in a heavenly calling, consider Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession,
verses.after: Therefore, holy brothers and sisters, partners in a heavenly calling, consider Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, holy brothers, sharers in a heavenly calling, consider Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession,

verses.rationale: Keeps appointment, Moses and house comparison.
verses.before: who was faithful to him who appointed him, just as Moses also was faithful in all God’s house.
verses.after: He was faithful to the one who appointed him, just as Moses was in all God's house.
verses.tsw_comparator: who was faithful to him who appointed him, just as Moses also was faithful in all God’s house.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit comparison and builder analogy.
verses.before: For Jesus has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses—as much more glory as the builder of a house has more honor than the house itself.
verses.after: For Jesus has been considered worthy of more glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has more honor than the house itself.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Jesus has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses—as much more glory as the builder of a house has more honor than the house itself.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal house logic and divine conclusion.
verses.before: For every house is built by someone, but the builder of everything is God.
verses.after: Every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: For every house is built by someone, but the builder of all things is God.

verses.rationale: Preserves servant status and forward-looking witness.
verses.before: Now Moses was faithful in all God’s house as a servant, to testify to the things that were to be spoken later,
verses.after: Moses was faithful as a servant in all God's house, testifying to what would be spoken later.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Moses was faithful in all God’s house as a servant, to testify to the things that were to be spoken later,

verses.rationale: Keeps Son/servant contrast, communal house and condition.
verses.before: but Christ is faithful over God’s house as a son. And we are his house, if indeed we hold firmly our confidence and our boasting in hope.
verses.after: But Christ is faithful as a Son over God's house. And we are his house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope in which we boast.
verses.tsw_comparator: but Christ is faithful over God’s house as a son. And we are his house, if indeed we hold fast our confidence and our boasting in hope.

verses.rationale: Attributes the present scriptural voice to the Spirit and retains today.
verses.before: So, as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear his voice,
verses.after: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear his voice,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear his voice,

verses.rationale: Keeps heart-hardening, rebellion and wilderness.
verses.before: do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
verses.after: do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
verses.tsw_comparator: do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness,

verses.rationale: Preserves ancestral testing and divine first-person speech.
verses.before: where your fathers put me to the test and saw my works for forty years.
verses.after: where your ancestors tested and tried me and saw my works
verses.tsw_comparator: where your fathers put me to the test and saw my works for forty years.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact duration, anger and inward wandering.
verses.before: So I was provoked with that generation, and said, ‘They always go astray in their heart; they have not known my ways.’
verses.after: for forty years. Therefore, I was angry with that generation and said, ‘They always wander in their hearts, and they have not known my ways.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I was provoked with that generation, and said, ‘They always go astray in their heart; they have not known my ways.’

verses.rationale: Renders the oath idiom as emphatic exclusion while preserving anger and rest.
verses.before: As I swore in my wrath, ‘They shall not enter my rest.’”
verses.after: So I swore in my anger, ‘They will never enter my rest.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: As I swore in my wrath, ‘They shall not enter my rest.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps corporate vigilance and apostasy movement.
verses.before: Take care, brothers and sisters, lest there be in any of you an evil, unbelieving heart, leading you to fall away from the living God.
verses.after: Watch out, brothers and sisters, that none of you has an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take care, brothers, lest there be in any of you an evil, unbelieving heart, leading you to fall away from the living God.

verses.rationale: Retains daily reciprocity, repeated today and deceptive hardening.
verses.before: But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called “today,” that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
verses.after: Instead, encourage one another every day, as long as it is called “Today,” so that none of you may be hardened by sin's deception.
verses.tsw_comparator: But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called “today,” that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.

verses.rationale: Keeps participation and persevering condition.
verses.before: For we have come to share in Christ, if indeed we hold our original confidence firm to the end.
verses.after: For we have become partners of Christ, if we hold our original confidence firm to the end.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we have come to share in Christ, if indeed we hold our original confidence firm to the end.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated quotation as active warning.
verses.before: As it is said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”
verses.after: As it is said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”
verses.tsw_comparator: As it is said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical question, exodus and Moses.
verses.before: For who were people who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not all people who left Egypt led by Moses?
verses.after: For who heard and rebelled? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt under Moses?
verses.tsw_comparator: For who were those who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not all those who left Egypt led by Moses?

verses.rationale: Retains exact duration and the stark image of corpses.
verses.before: And with whom was he provoked for forty years? Was it not with people who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
verses.after: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
verses.tsw_comparator: And with whom was he provoked for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

verses.rationale: Keeps oath, rest and disobedience.
verses.before: And to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, but to people who were disobedient?
verses.after: And to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, if not to those who disobeyed?
verses.tsw_comparator: And to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, but to those who were disobedient?

verses.rationale: Preserves the concluding cause.
verses.before: So we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief.
verses.after: So we see that they could not enter because of unbelief.
verses.tsw_comparator: So we see that they were unable to enter because of unbelief.

verses.rationale: Keeps continuing promise, communal fear and race-like shortfall.
verses.before: So, while the promise of entering God’s rest still stands, let us fear lest any of you should seem to have fallen short of it.
verses.after: Therefore, since the promise of entering his rest remains, let us fear that any one of you may appear to have fallen short.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, while the promise of entering God’s rest still stands, let us fear lest any of you should seem to have fallen short of it.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned united-with-hearers reading and preserves comparison.
verses.before: For good news was proclaimed to us just as it was to them; but the message they heard did not benefit them, because it was not united with trust in people who heard.
verses.after: For we too have received good news just as they did, but the message they heard did not benefit them because they were not united by faith with those who listened.
verses.tsw_comparator: For good news was proclaimed to us just as it was to them; but the message they heard did not benefit them, because it was not united with trust in those who heard.

verses.rationale: Keeps present entry, oath and creation completion.
verses.before: For we who have trusted enter that rest, just as God has said, “As I swore in my wrath, ‘They will not enter my rest,’” although God’s works were finished from the foundation of the world.
verses.after: For we who have believed enter the rest, just as he said, “So I swore in my anger, ‘They will never enter my rest,’” though his works were finished from the foundation of the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we who have trusted enter that rest, just as God has said, “As I swore in my wrath, ‘They shall not enter my rest,’” although God’s works were finished from the foundation of the world.

verses.rationale: Retains indefinite citation and exact day.
verses.before: For somewhere it is spoken about the seventh day in this way: “And God rested on the seventh day from all his works.”
verses.after: For somewhere he has spoken about the seventh day this way: “And God rested on the seventh day from all his works.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For somewhere it is spoken about the seventh day in this way: “And God rested on the seventh day from all his works.”

verses.rationale: Keeps repetition and exclusion.
verses.before: And again in this passage God said, “They will not enter my rest.”
verses.after: And again in this passage, “They will never enter my rest.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And again in this passage God said, “They shall not enter my rest.”

verses.rationale: Preserves open opportunity and earlier failure.
verses.before: Since therefore it remains for some to enter it, and people who formerly received the good news failed to enter because of disobedience,
verses.after: Therefore, since it remains for some to enter it, and those who previously received the good news did not enter because of disobedience,
verses.tsw_comparator: Since therefore it remains for some to enter it, and those who formerly received the good news failed to enter because of disobedience,

verses.rationale: Keeps named David, delayed today and repeated warning.
verses.before: again God appoints a certain day—“Today”—saying through David so long afterward, in the words already quoted, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
verses.after: God again appoints a certain day—“Today”—speaking through David after so long a time, as quoted above: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
verses.tsw_comparator: again God appoints a certain day—“Today”—saying through David so long afterward, in the words already quoted, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”

verses.rationale: Uses Joshua to distinguish the Greek name from Jesus in context.
verses.before: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
verses.after: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.

verses.rationale: Retains the rare Sabbath-rest noun.
verses.before: So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God,
verses.after: So a Sabbath rest remains for God's people.
verses.tsw_comparator: So then, a Sabbath rest remains for the people of God,

verses.rationale: Keeps human/divine analogy.
verses.before: for whoever has entered God’s rest has also rested from their works as God did from his.
verses.after: For whoever enters God's rest also rests from their works, just as God did from his.
verses.tsw_comparator: for whoever has entered God’s rest has also rested from their works as God did from his.

verses.rationale: Preserves urgent effort and fall pattern.
verses.before: Let us therefore make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one may fall by the same pattern of disobedience.
verses.after: Therefore, let us make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one falls by following the same pattern of disobedience.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us therefore make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one may fall by the same pattern of disobedience.

verses.rationale: Keeps violent cutting image, all paired inner terms and judgment.
verses.before: For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing to the dividing of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
verses.after: For God's word is living and active, sharper than any double-edged sword, penetrating to the division of soul and spirit, joints and marrow, and judging the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing to the dividing of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and discerning the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

verses.rationale: Preserves exposure, divine sight and accountability.
verses.before: And no creature is hidden from God’s sight, but all are naked and laid bare to the eyes of the one to whom we must give account.
verses.after: No creature is hidden before him; everything is naked and exposed to the eyes of the one to whom we must give account.
verses.tsw_comparator: And no creature is hidden from God’s sight, but all are naked and laid bare to the eyes of the one to whom we must give account.

verses.rationale: Keeps heavenly passage, full identity and perseverance.
verses.before: Since then we have a great priest who has passed through the heavens—Jesus, the Son of God—let us hold firmly our confession.
verses.after: Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens—Jesus, God's Son—let us hold firmly to our confession.
verses.tsw_comparator: Since then we have a great priest who has passed through the heavens—Jesus, the Son of God—let us hold fast our confession.

verses.rationale: Preserves sympathy, comprehensive testing and sinlessness.
verses.before: For we do not have a priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every way has been tested as we are, yet without sin.
verses.after: For we do not have a high priest unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who has been tested in every way as we are, yet without sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we do not have a priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every way has been tested as we are, yet without sin.

verses.rationale: Keeps throne image, bold access and needed aid.
verses.before: Let us therefore approach with confidence to the throne of grace, so that we may receive mercy and find grace for timely help.
verses.after: So let us approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace for timely help.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us therefore draw near with confidence to the throne of grace, so that we may receive mercy and find grace for timely help.

verses.rationale: Preserves human origin, representation and both offerings.
verses.before: For every high priest chosen from among mortals is appointed on behalf of mortals in matters pertaining to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
verses.after: Every high priest chosen from among human beings is appointed on their behalf in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: For every high priest chosen from among mortals is appointed on behalf of mortals in matters pertaining to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.

verses.rationale: Keeps measured compassion and surrounding weakness image.
verses.before: The high priest can deal gently with the ignorant and the wayward, since the high priest is also surrounded by weakness.
verses.after: He is able to deal gently with the ignorant and wandering because he himself is clothed with weakness.
verses.tsw_comparator: The high priest is able to deal gently with the ignorant and the wayward, since the high priest is also surrounded by weakness.

verses.rationale: Retains priestly liability and parallel offerings.
verses.before: And because of this, the high priest is obligated to offer sacrifices for their own sins as well as for the people.
verses.after: Because of this weakness, he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins as well as for the people's.
verses.tsw_comparator: And because of this, the high priest is obligated to offer sacrifices for their own sins as well as for the people.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine call and named precedent.
verses.before: And no one takes this honor upon themselves, but only when called by God, just as Aaron was.
verses.after: No one takes this honor for himself but receives it when called by God, just as Aaron was.
verses.tsw_comparator: And no one takes this honor upon themselves, but only when called by God, just as Aaron was.

verses.rationale: Preserves denied self-exaltation and filial quotation.
verses.before: So also Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest, but was appointed by the one who said to him, “You are my Son; today I have begotten you,”
verses.after: In the same way, Christ did not glorify himself by becoming high priest. Instead, God said to him, “You are my Son; today I have fathered you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So also Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest, but was appointed by the one who said to him, “You are my Son; today I have begotten you,”

verses.rationale: Keeps eternal priesthood and unexplained named order.
verses.before: just as God says also in another place, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
verses.after: As he also says elsewhere, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
verses.tsw_comparator: just as God says also in another place, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”

verses.rationale: Retains embodied life, emotional intensity and the difficult heard-despite-death claim.
verses.before: In the days of his flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears, to the one who could save him from death; and he was heard because of his reverent devotion.
verses.after: During the days of his flesh, he offered prayers and pleas, with loud cries and tears, to the one able to save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverent submission.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the days of his flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears, to the one who was able to save him from death; and he was heard because of his reverent devotion.

verses.rationale: Keeps sonship, learning and suffering.
verses.before: Although he was a Son, he learned obedience through what he suffered.
verses.after: Although he was a Son, he learned obedience through what he suffered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Although he was a Son, he learned obedience through what he suffered.

verses.rationale: Preserves perfection/completion and obedience.
verses.before: And having been made complete, he became the source of eternal salvation for everyone who obey him,
verses.after: And having been perfected, he became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey him,
verses.tsw_comparator: And having been made complete, he became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey him,

verses.rationale: Retains divine designation and repeated order.
verses.before: being designated by God a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
verses.after: having been designated by God a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
verses.tsw_comparator: being designated by God a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.

verses.rationale: Keeps pedagogical difficulty located in listeners.
verses.before: About this we have much to say, and it is hard to explain, since you have become dull in hearing.
verses.after: We have much to say about this, but it is difficult to explain because you have become sluggish in hearing.
verses.tsw_comparator: About this we have much to say, and it is hard to explain, since you have become dull in hearing.

verses.rationale: Preserves rebuke, elemental basics and diet metaphor.
verses.before: For though by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to teach you again the basic principles of the beginning of the words of God. You need milk, not solid food.
verses.after: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you again need someone to teach you the basic elements of God's sayings. You have come to need milk, not solid food.
verses.tsw_comparator: For though by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to teach you again the basic principles of the beginning of the words of God. You need milk, not solid food.

verses.rationale: Keeps infancy and inexperience.
verses.before: For everyone who lives on milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, since they are a child.
verses.after: Everyone who lives on milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, since such a person is an infant.
verses.tsw_comparator: For everyone who lives on milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, since they are a child.

verses.rationale: Retains trained perception and moral discernment.
verses.before: But solid food is for the mature—for those whose powers of discernment have been trained by practice to distinguish good from evil.
verses.after: But solid food is for the mature, whose senses have been trained by practice to distinguish good from evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: But solid food is for the mature—for those whose powers of discernment have been trained by practice to distinguish good from evil.

verses.rationale: Keeps movement toward maturity and the first two foundation elements.
verses.before: So let us leave the elementary teaching about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God,
verses.after: Therefore, let us move beyond the elementary message about Christ and be carried on toward maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and faith in God,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore let us leave the elementary teaching about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God,

verses.rationale: Preserves plural washings and the remaining four teachings.
verses.before: and of instruction about washings, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
verses.after: instruction about washings, laying on of hands, resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: and of instruction about washings, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.

verses.rationale: Keeps intention under divine permission.
verses.before: And this we will do if God permits.
verses.after: And we will do this, if God permits.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this we will do if God permits.

verses.rationale: Retains the severe impossibility and first three experiences.
verses.before: For it is impossible, in the case of people who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, and have shared in the Holy Spirit,
verses.after: For it is impossible to restore again to repentance those who were once enlightened, tasted the heavenly gift, became partners in the Holy Spirit,
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, and have shared in the Holy Spirit,

verses.rationale: Keeps tasting and future-power experience.
verses.before: and have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the age to come,
verses.after: tasted God's good word and the powers of the coming age,
verses.tsw_comparator: and have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the age to come,

verses.rationale: Preserves apostasy, recrucifixion and public humiliation.
verses.before: and then have fallen away, to restore them again to repentance, since they are crucifying once again the Son of God to their own harm and holding him up to contempt.
verses.after: and then fell away, since they crucify God's Son again for themselves and expose him to public shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: and then have fallen away, to restore them again to repentance, since they are crucifying once again the Son of God to their own harm and holding him up to contempt.

verses.rationale: Keeps agricultural analogy, repeated rain and useful yield.
verses.before: For land that has drunk the rain that often falls on it, and produces a crop useful to those for whose sake it is cultivated, receives a blessing from God,
verses.after: For land that drinks the rain falling on it again and again and produces a useful crop for those who cultivate it receives blessing from God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For land that has drunk the rain that often falls on it, and produces a crop useful to those for whose sake it is cultivated, receives a blessing from God,

verses.rationale: Retains failed crop, curse and fire.
verses.before: but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is worthless and near to being cursed, and its end is to be burned.
verses.after: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless and near a curse; its end is burning.
verses.tsw_comparator: but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is worthless and near to being cursed, and its end is to be burned.

verses.rationale: Keeps warning balanced by affectionate confidence.
verses.before: Though we speak in this way, beloved, we feel sure of better things—things that belong to salvation.
verses.after: But even though we speak this way, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case—things belonging to salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though we speak in this way, beloved, we feel sure of better things—things that belong to salvation.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine memory and past/present service.
verses.before: For God is not unjust so as to overlook your work and the love that you have shown for his name in serving the saints, as you still do.
verses.after: For God is not unjust; he will not forget your work and the love you showed for his name by serving the saints, as you still do.
verses.tsw_comparator: For God is not unjust so as to overlook your work and the love that you have shown for his name in serving the saints, as you still do.

verses.rationale: Keeps individual scope, persistence and assurance.
verses.before: And we desire each person of you to show the same diligence to the full assurance of hope until the end,
verses.after: We desire each of you to show the same diligence until the end, so as to have full assurance of hope,
verses.tsw_comparator: And we desire each one of you to show the same diligence to the full assurance of hope until the end,

verses.rationale: Retains warning, imitation and twin means.
verses.before: so that you may not be sluggish, but imitators of people who through trust and patience inherit the promises.
verses.after: so that you do not become sluggish but imitate those who inherit the promises through faith and patience.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may not be sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.

verses.rationale: Keeps named patriarch and divine self-oath.
verses.before: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he had no one greater by whom to swear, he swore by himself,
verses.after: When God made his promise to Abraham, since he had no one greater by whom to swear, he swore by himself,
verses.tsw_comparator: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he had no one greater by whom to swear, he swore by himself,

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic doubled Hebrew idioms.
verses.before: saying, “Surely I will bless you and multiply you.”
verses.after: saying, “Surely I will bless you greatly and multiply you greatly.”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “Surely I will bless you and multiply you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps endurance and fulfillment.
verses.before: And thus Abraham, having patiently waited, obtained the promise.
verses.after: And so, after patiently waiting, Abraham obtained the promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: And thus Abraham, having patiently waited, obtained the promise.

verses.rationale: Retains social oath logic and finality.
verses.before: For people swear by something greater than themselves, and in all their disputes an oath is final for confirmation.
verses.after: For people swear by someone greater, and the oath confirms the matter and ends every dispute for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For people swear by something greater than themselves, and in all their disputes an oath is final for confirmation.

verses.rationale: Keeps heirs, immutability and divine guarantee.
verses.before: So when God desired to show more convincingly to the heirs of the promise the unchangeable character of his purpose, he guaranteed it with an oath,
verses.after: In the same way, because God wanted to show the heirs of the promise more clearly the unchangeable nature of his purpose, he guaranteed it with an oath,
verses.tsw_comparator: So when God desired to show more convincingly to the heirs of the promise the unchangeable character of his purpose, he guaranteed it with an oath,

verses.rationale: Preserves impossibility, refuge and gripping hope.
verses.before: so that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to hold firmly to the hope set before us.
verses.after: so that through two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to seize the hope set before us.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before us.

verses.rationale: Keeps anchor and sanctuary imagery together.
verses.before: We have this as a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters into the inner place behind the curtain,
verses.after: We have this hope as a secure and firm anchor for the soul, entering the inner place behind the curtain,
verses.tsw_comparator: We have this as a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters into the inner place behind the curtain,

verses.rationale: Retains forerunner, representation and eternal named priesthood.
verses.before: where Jesus has gone as a forerunner on our behalf, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
verses.after: where Jesus entered ahead of us on our behalf, having become high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
verses.tsw_comparator: where Jesus has gone as a forerunner on our behalf, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.

verses.rationale: Preserves all titles, names and military setting.
verses.before: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
verses.after: This Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, met Abraham as he returned from defeating the kings and blessed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,

verses.rationale: Keeps tithe and both etymological interpretations.
verses.before: and to him Abraham apportioned a tenth of everything. He is first, by translation of his name, king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, that is, king of peace.
verses.after: Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. His name first means “king of righteousness,” and then “king of Salem,” that is, “king of peace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and to him Abraham apportioned a tenth of everything. He is first, by translation of his name, king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, that is, king of peace.

verses.rationale: Retains the narrative's genealogical silence as stated and the Son resemblance.
verses.before: He is without father or mother or genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God he continues a priest forever.
verses.after: Without father, mother or genealogy, with neither beginning of days nor end of life, resembling God's Son, he remains a priest continually.
verses.tsw_comparator: He is without father or mother or genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God he continues a priest forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps greatness, patriarch title and war spoils.
verses.before: See how great this man was to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth of the spoils!
verses.after: Consider how great he was: even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the spoils.
verses.tsw_comparator: See how great this man was to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth of the spoils!

verses.rationale: Preserves legal tithe, kinship and bodily descent.
verses.before: And those descendants of Levi who receive the priestly office have a commandment in the law to take tithes from the people, that is, from their brothers and sisters, though these also are descended from Abraham.
verses.after: Now those descendants of Levi who receive the priesthood have a command in the law to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their own brothers and sisters—even though they too come from Abraham's body.
verses.tsw_comparator: And those descendants of Levi who receive the priestly office have a commandment in the law to take tithes from the people, that is, from their brothers, though these also are descended from Abraham.

verses.rationale: Keeps contrast, tithe and promise-holder.
verses.before: But this man, who does not trace his descent from them, received tithes from Abraham and blessed the one who had the promises.
verses.after: But Melchizedek, whose genealogy is not traced from them, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed the one who had the promises.
verses.tsw_comparator: But this man, who does not trace his descent from them, received tithes from Abraham and blessed the one who had the promises.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit hierarchy.
verses.before: It is beyond dispute that the inferior is blessed by the superior.
verses.after: Without any dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is beyond dispute that the inferior is blessed by the superior.

verses.rationale: Keeps mortal/living contrast grounded in testimony.
verses.before: In the one case tithes are received by mortal men, but in the other case, by one of whom it is testified that he lives.
verses.after: In the one case, mortal people receive tithes; in the other, one receives them who is testified to be living.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the one case tithes are received by mortal men, but in the other case, by one of whom it is testified that he lives.

verses.rationale: Preserves the author's qualifying phrase and corporate ancestry.
verses.before: One might even say that Levi himself, who receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham,
verses.after: One might even say that Levi, who receives tithes, paid a tithe through Abraham,
verses.tsw_comparator: One might even say that Levi himself, who receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham,

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily descent logic and meeting.
verses.before: for he was still in the loins of his ancestor when Melchizedek met him.
verses.after: for he was still in his ancestor's body when Melchizedek met Abraham.
verses.tsw_comparator: for he was still in the loins of his ancestor when Melchizedek met him.

verses.rationale: Preserves counterfactual, legal relation and both named orders.
verses.before: Now if perfection had been attainable through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people received the law), what further need would there have been for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, rather than one named after the order of Aaron?
verses.after: Now if perfection had come through the Levitical priesthood—for on its basis the people received the law—what further need was there for another priest to arise according to Melchizedek's order rather than Aaron's?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now if perfection had been attainable through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people received the law), what further need would there have been for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, rather than one named after the order of Aaron?

verses.rationale: Keeps stated necessary legal consequence.
verses.before: For when there is a change in the priesthood, there is necessarily a change in the law as well.
verses.after: For when the priesthood is changed, a change of law necessarily follows.
verses.tsw_comparator: For when there is a change in the priesthood, there is necessarily a change in the law as well.

verses.rationale: Retains tribal distinction and cultic service.
verses.before: For the one of whom these things are spoken belonged to another tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
verses.after: The one about whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one served at the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the one of whom these things are spoken belonged to another tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps Judah, Moses and scriptural silence.
verses.before: For it is evident that our Lord was descended from Judah, and in connection with that tribe Moses said nothing about priests.
verses.after: For it is evident that our Lord arose from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is evident that our Lord was descended from Judah, and in connection with that tribe Moses said nothing about priests.

verses.rationale: Preserves rising and likeness.
verses.before: This becomes even more evident when another priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,
verses.after: This becomes even clearer when another priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,
verses.tsw_comparator: This becomes even more evident when another priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,

verses.rationale: Keeps fleshly-command contrast and indestructible life.
verses.before: who has become a priest, not on the basis of a legal requirement concerning bodily descent, but by the power of an indestructible life.
verses.after: one who became priest not according to a law based on physical descent but according to the power of an indestructible life.
verses.tsw_comparator: who has become a priest, not on the basis of a legal requirement concerning bodily descent, but by the power of an indestructible life.

verses.rationale: Retains quotation as evidence.
verses.before: For it is witnessed of him, “You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.”
verses.after: For it is testified, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is witnessed of him, “You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.”

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit annulment and negative evaluation.
verses.before: For on the one hand, a former commandment is set aside because of its weakness and uselessness
verses.after: On the one hand, a former command is set aside because it was weak and ineffective,
verses.tsw_comparator: For on the one hand, a former commandment is set aside because of its weakness and uselessness

verses.rationale: Preserves contrast, better hope and access.
verses.before: (for the law made nothing perfect), but on the other hand a better hope is introduced, through which we approach to God.
verses.after: for the law perfected nothing. On the other hand, a better hope is introduced, through which we draw near to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: (for the law made nothing perfect), but on the other hand a better hope is introduced, through which we draw near to God.

verses.rationale: Keeps oath contrast and continuity into next verse.
verses.before: And it was not without an oath. For people who formerly became priests were made such without an oath,
verses.after: And this was not done without an oath. Others became priests without an oath,
verses.tsw_comparator: And it was not without an oath. For those who formerly became priests were made such without an oath,

verses.rationale: Preserves irrevocable divine oath.
verses.before: but this one was made a priest with an oath by the one who said to him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind, ‘You are a priest forever.’”
verses.after: but he became priest with an oath through the one who said to him, “The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: but this one was made a priest with an oath by the one who said to him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind, ‘You are a priest forever.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps personal name, legal guarantee and comparison.
verses.before: This makes Jesus the guarantor of a better covenant.
verses.after: Accordingly, Jesus has become the guarantor of a better covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: This makes Jesus the guarantor of a better covenant.

verses.rationale: Retains mortality as reason for succession.
verses.before: The former priests were many in number, because they were prevented by death from continuing in office,
verses.after: There have been many priests because death prevented them from continuing in office,
verses.tsw_comparator: The former priests were many in number, because they were prevented by death from continuing in office,

verses.rationale: Keeps permanence and enduring tenure.
verses.before: but he holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever.
verses.after: but because Jesus remains forever, he holds a permanent priesthood.
verses.tsw_comparator: but he holds his priesthood permanently, because he continues forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive salvation, access and continuing intercession.
verses.before: Consequently, he can save completely people who approach to God through him, since he always lives to intercede for them.
verses.after: Therefore, he is able to save completely those who approach God through him, since he always lives to intercede for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Consequently, he is able to save completely those who draw near to God through him, since he always lives to intercede for them.

verses.rationale: Keeps all five descriptions, including separation.
verses.before: For it was fitting that we should have such a high priest, holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
verses.after: For this is the kind of high priest we needed: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners and exalted above the heavens.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it was fitting that we should have such a high priest, holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.

verses.rationale: Preserves comparison, self-offering and once-for-all claim.
verses.before: He has no need, like those high priests, to offer sacrifices daily, first for his own sins and then for those of the people, since he did this once for all when he offered up himself.
verses.after: He does not need to offer sacrifices every day, like the high priests—first for his own sins and then for the people's—because he did this once for all when he offered himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: He has no need, like those high priests, to offer sacrifices daily, first for his own sins and then for those of the people, since he did this once for all when he offered up himself.

verses.rationale: Keeps law/oath contrast, weakness and eternal Son.
verses.before: For the law appoints men in their weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came later than the law, appoints a Son who has been made perfect forever.
verses.after: For the law appoints as high priests people who have weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son who has been perfected forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the law appoints men in their weakness as high priests, but the word of the oath, which came later than the law, appoints a Son who has been made perfect forever.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit main point, enthronement and heaven.
verses.before: Now the point in what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, one who is seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,
verses.after: The main point of what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the Majesty's throne in heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the point in what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, one who is seated at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,

verses.rationale: Keeps cultic service and divine construction.
verses.before: a minister in the sanctuary and in the true tent that the Lord set up, not man.
verses.after: He is a minister in the holy place and in the true tent, which the Lord set up, not a human being.
verses.tsw_comparator: a minister in the sanctuary and in the true tent that the Lord set up, not man.

verses.rationale: Preserves priestly necessity and open referent.
verses.before: For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; thus it is necessary for this one also to have something to offer.
verses.after: Every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices, so this one too must have something to offer.
verses.tsw_comparator: For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; thus it is necessary for this one also to have something to offer.

verses.rationale: Keeps counterfactual and existing legal service.
verses.before: Now if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, since there are priests who offer gifts according to the law.
verses.after: If he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, since there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, since there are priests who offer gifts according to the law.

verses.rationale: Retains copy/shadow, Moses, mountain and pattern.
verses.before: They serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things. For when Moses was about to erect the tent, he was instructed by God, saying, “See that you make everything according to the pattern that was shown you on the mountain.”
verses.after: They serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was warned when he was about to complete the tent: “See that you make everything according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things. For when Moses was about to erect the tent, he was instructed by God, saying, “See that you make everything according to the pattern that was shown you on the mountain.”

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated better language and legal establishment.
verses.before: But as it is, he has obtained a ministry that is as much more excellent than the old as the covenant he mediates is better, since it is enacted on better promises.
verses.after: But now Jesus has obtained a more excellent ministry, just as he is mediator of a better covenant enacted on better promises.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as it is, he has obtained a ministry that is as much more excellent than the old as the covenant he mediates is better, since it is enacted on better promises.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional comparative logic.
verses.before: For if that first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no occasion to look for a second.
verses.after: For if that first covenant had been faultless, no place would have been sought for a second.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if that first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no occasion to look for a second.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned ‘them’ reading and retains both named houses.
verses.before: For he finds fault with them when he says: “Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,
verses.after: But finding fault with them, God says, “Look, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he finds fault with them when he says: “Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

verses.rationale: Keeps handholding exodus image, failure and divine response.
verses.before: not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, for they did not continue in my covenant, and so I showed no concern for them, declares the Lord.
verses.after: It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt, because they did not remain in my covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, for they did not continue in my covenant, and so I showed no concern for them, declares the Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves inward writing and reciprocal covenant relation.
verses.before: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord: I will put my laws into their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
verses.after: For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws into their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord: I will put my laws into their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal knowledge and social range.
verses.before: And they will not teach, each person his neighbor and each one his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest.
verses.after: No one will teach a fellow citizen or a brother or sister, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know me, from the least to the greatest.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they shall not teach, each one his neighbor and each one his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest.

verses.rationale: Retains mercy and deliberate nonremembrance.
verses.before: For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more.”
verses.after: For I will be merciful toward their wrongdoings and will remember their sins no more.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more.”

verses.rationale: Keeps aging/disappearance imagery and temporal process.
verses.before: In speaking of a new covenant, he makes the first obsolete. And what is becoming obsolete and growing old is ready to vanish away.
verses.after: By speaking of a “new” covenant, he has made the first obsolete; and what is becoming obsolete and growing old is near disappearance.
verses.tsw_comparator: In speaking of a new covenant, he makes the first obsolete. And what is becoming obsolete and growing old is ready to vanish away.

verses.rationale: Retains first-covenant setting, worship and earthly holy place.
verses.before: Now even the first covenant had regulations for worship and an earthly place of holiness.
verses.after: Now the first covenant also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now even the first covenant had regulations for worship and an earthly place of holiness.

verses.rationale: Keeps furnishings and named area.
verses.before: For a tent was prepared, the first section, in which were the lampstand and the table and the bread of the Presence. It is called the Holy Place.
verses.after: A tent was prepared. In its first section were the lampstand, the table and the presented bread; this section is called the Holy Place.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a tent was prepared, the first section, in which were the lampstand and the table and the bread of the Presence. It is called the Holy Place.

verses.rationale: Preserves spatial sequence and title.
verses.before: Behind the second curtain was a second section called the Most Holy Place,
verses.after: Behind the second curtain was a section of the tent called the Most Holy Place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behind the second curtain was a second section called the Most Holy Place,

verses.rationale: Keeps every object, material and named Aaron.
verses.before: having the golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant covered on all sides with gold, in which was a golden jar holding the manna, and Aaron’s staff that budded, and the tablets of the covenant.
verses.after: It had the golden incense altar and the ark of the covenant covered completely with gold. In the ark were a gold jar holding the manna, Aaron's staff that had budded and the tablets of the covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: having the golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant covered on all sides with gold, in which was a golden jar holding the manna, and Aaron’s staff that budded, and the tablets of the covenant.

verses.rationale: Retains winged beings, cover and author's restraint.
verses.before: Above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. Of these things we cannot now speak in detail.
verses.after: Above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the atonement cover. We cannot now discuss these things in detail.
verses.tsw_comparator: Above it were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. Of these things we cannot now speak in detail.

verses.rationale: Keeps recurring access and priestly work.
verses.before: These preparations having thus been made, the priests go regularly into the first section, performing their ritual duties,
verses.after: With these things arranged this way, the priests continually enter the first section of the tent to perform their services.
verses.tsw_comparator: These preparations having thus been made, the priests go regularly into the first section, performing their ritual duties,

verses.rationale: Preserves exclusivity, exact frequency, blood and unintended sins.
verses.before: but into the second only the high priest goes, and he but once a year, and not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the unintentional sins of the people.
verses.after: But only the high priest enters the second section, and only once a year, never without blood, which he offers for himself and for the people's sins committed in ignorance.
verses.tsw_comparator: but into the second only the high priest goes, and he but once a year, and not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the unintentional sins of the people.

verses.rationale: Keeps Spirit's interpretive agency and blocked access.
verses.before: By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places is not yet opened as long as the first section is still standing
verses.after: By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy place has not yet been disclosed while the first tent is still standing.
verses.tsw_comparator: By this the Holy Spirit indicates that the way into the holy places is not yet opened as long as the first section is still standing

verses.rationale: Retains parable/illustration and conscience limitation.
verses.before: (which is symbolic for the present age). According to this arrangement, gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the conscience of the worshiper,
verses.after: This is an illustration for the present time, in which gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper's conscience.
