verses.rationale: Keeps the limited categories and temporary imposition.
verses.before: but deal only with food and drink and various washings, regulations for the body imposed until the time of reformation.
verses.after: They concern only food, drink and various washings—physical regulations imposed until a time of reformation.
verses.tsw_comparator: but deal only with food and drink and various washings, regulations for the body imposed until the time of reformation.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned ‘have come’ reading and keeps uncreated tent.
verses.before: But when Christ appeared as a high priest of the good things that have come, then through the greater and more perfect tent (not made with hands, that is, not of this creation)
verses.after: But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come, he passed through the greater and more perfect tent not made by hands, that is, not of this creation.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Christ appeared as a high priest of the good things that have come, then through the greater and more perfect tent (not made with hands, that is, not of this creation)

verses.rationale: Preserves animal/his-own contrast, blood and finality.
verses.before: he entered once for all into the holy places, not by means of the blood of goats and calves but by means of his own blood, thus securing an eternal redemption.
verses.after: He entered the holy place once for all, not by the blood of goats and calves but by his own blood, obtaining eternal redemption.
verses.tsw_comparator: he entered once for all into the holy places, not by means of the blood of goats and calves but by means of his own blood, thus securing an eternal redemption.

verses.rationale: Keeps all ritual substances and conditional claim.
verses.before: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the sprinkling of defiled persons with the ashes of a heifer, sanctify for the purification of the flesh,
verses.after: For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are defiled make them holy for outward cleansing,
verses.tsw_comparator: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the sprinkling of defiled persons with the ashes of a heifer, sanctify for the purification of the flesh,

verses.rationale: Retains comparison, Spirit, self-offering and conscience purpose.
verses.before: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to serve the living God.
verses.after: how much more will Christ's blood, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works so that we may serve the living God?
verses.tsw_comparator: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to serve the living God.

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant mediation, death, redemption and inheritance.
verses.before: So he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that people who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, since a death has occurred that redeems them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant.
verses.after: For this reason Christ is mediator of a new covenant, so that, since a death has occurred to redeem transgressions under the first covenant, those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, since a death has occurred that redeems them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant.

verses.rationale: Carries the covenant/will wordplay into testamentary logic.
verses.before: For where a covenant is, there must of necessity be the death of the one who made it.
verses.after: For where there is a will, the death of the one who made it must be established.
verses.tsw_comparator: For where a covenant is, there must of necessity be the death of the one who made it.

verses.rationale: Preserves legal explanation.
verses.before: For a covenant is established only at death, since it is not in force as long as the one who made it is alive.
verses.after: A will is valid only after death; it never takes effect while the one who made it is living.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a covenant is established only at death, since it is not in force as long as the one who made it is alive.

verses.rationale: Keeps negative emphasis and inauguration.
verses.before: So not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood.
verses.after: Therefore, not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood.

verses.rationale: Retains Moses, every ritual material and both objects sprinkled.
verses.before: For when every commandment of the law had been declared by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
verses.after: After Moses had spoken every command of the law to all the people, he took the blood of calves with water, scarlet wool and hyssop and sprinkled the scroll itself and all the people,
verses.tsw_comparator: For when every commandment of the law had been declared by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,

verses.rationale: Keeps blood-covenant formula and divine command.
verses.before: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you.”
verses.after: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive ritual blood application.
verses.before: And in the same way he sprinkled with the blood both the tent and all the vessels used in worship.
verses.after: In the same way, he sprinkled the tent and all the vessels used in worship with blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: And in the same way he sprinkled with the blood both the tent and all the vessels used in worship.

verses.rationale: Keeps qualifying almost and the violent condition.
verses.before: Indeed, under the law almost everything is purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness of sins.
verses.after: Indeed, under the law almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without blood being poured out there is no forgiveness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, under the law almost everything is purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness of sins.

verses.rationale: Retains startling heavenly cleansing and comparative offerings.
verses.before: Thus it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be purified with these rites, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
verses.after: Therefore, it was necessary for the copies of heavenly things to be cleansed with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be purified with these rites, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

verses.rationale: Keeps copy/true contrast and representative divine presence.
verses.before: For Christ has entered, not into holy places made with hands, which are copies of the true things, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf.
verses.after: For Christ did not enter a holy place made by hands, a copy of the true one, but heaven itself, now to appear before God's face on our behalf.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Christ has entered, not into holy places made with hands, which are copies of the true things, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated annual contrast and other's blood.
verses.before: Nor was it to offer himself repeatedly, as the high priest enters the holy places every year with blood not his own,
verses.after: Nor did he enter to offer himself again and again, as the high priest enters the holy place every year with blood not his own.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nor was it to offer himself repeatedly, as the high priest enters the holy places every year with blood not his own,

verses.rationale: Keeps counterfactual repeated suffering, final era and single self-sacrifice.
verses.before: for then he would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world. But as it is, he has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
verses.after: Otherwise, he would have had to suffer repeatedly since the world's foundation. But now he has appeared once at the culmination of the ages to abolish sin through his sacrifice.
verses.tsw_comparator: for then he would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world. But as it is, he has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.

verses.rationale: Retains universal appointment and sequence.
verses.before: And just as it is appointed for man to die once, and after that comes judgment,
verses.after: And just as human beings are appointed to die once, and after that comes judgment,
verses.tsw_comparator: And just as it is appointed for man to die once, and after that comes judgment,

verses.rationale: Keeps once/second contrast, sin-bearing and waiting community.
verses.before: so Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, not to deal with sin but to save people who are eagerly waiting for him.
verses.after: so Christ too, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time—not to deal with sin, but to bring salvation to those eagerly waiting for him.
verses.tsw_comparator: so Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, not to deal with sin but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him.

verses.rationale: Retains shadow/form and repeated sacrificial inability.
verses.before: For since the law has only a shadow of the good things to come, and not the true form of these realities, it can never—by the same sacrifices that are offered continually year after year—make people who approach complete.
verses.after: Since the law has only a shadow of the good things to come, not their true form, it can never perfect those who approach through the same sacrifices continually offered year after year.
verses.tsw_comparator: For since the law has only a shadow of the good things to come, and not the true form of these realities, it can never—by the same sacrifices that are offered continually year after year—make those who draw near complete.

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetorical counterfactual and conscience.
verses.before: Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, since the worshipers, having once been cleansed, would no longer have any awareness of sins?
verses.after: Otherwise, would they not have stopped being offered, since worshipers cleansed once would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
verses.tsw_comparator: Otherwise, would they not have ceased to be offered, since the worshipers, having once been cleansed, would no longer have any awareness of sins?

verses.rationale: Preserves annual remembrance.
verses.before: But in these sacrifices there is a reminder of sins year after year.
verses.after: But in those sacrifices there is a reminder of sins every year.
verses.tsw_comparator: But in these sacrifices there is a reminder of sins year after year.

verses.rationale: Keeps animal blood and explicit impossibility.
verses.before: For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
verses.after: For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

verses.rationale: Retains incarnation setting and the Greek body's prepared reading.
verses.before: So, when Christ came into the world, he said, “Sacrifices and offerings you did not desire, but a body you prepared for me.
verses.after: Therefore, when Christ comes into the world, he says, “You did not desire sacrifice and offering, but you prepared a body for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, when Christ came into the world, he said, “Sacrifices and offerings you did not desire, but a body you prepared for me.

verses.rationale: Keeps both sacrificial categories.
verses.before: In burnt offerings and offerings for sin you took no pleasure.
verses.after: You took no pleasure in burnt offerings and offerings for sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: In burnt offerings and offerings for sin you took no pleasure.

verses.rationale: Preserves arrival, scriptural scroll and divine will.
verses.before: Then I said, ‘Look—I have come to do your will, O God,’ as it is written of me in the scroll of the book.”
verses.after: Then I said, ‘Look, I have come—it is written about me in the scroll—to do your will, O God.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, ‘Look—I have come to do your will, O God,’ as it is written of me in the scroll of the book.”

verses.rationale: Keeps all four terms and legal qualification.
verses.before: When he said above, “You did not desire and you took no pleasure in sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings and offerings for sin” (these are offered according to the law),
verses.after: First he says, “You did not desire or take pleasure in sacrifices, offerings, burnt offerings and offerings for sin,” though these are offered according to the law.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he said above, “You did not desire and you took no pleasure in sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings and offerings for sin” (these are offered according to the law),

verses.rationale: Retains sequential interpretive conclusion.
verses.before: then he added, “Look—I have come to do your will.” He abolishes the first in order to establish the second.
verses.after: Then he says, “Look, I have come to do your will.” He sets aside the first in order to establish the second.
verses.tsw_comparator: then he added, “Look—I have come to do your will.” He abolishes the first in order to establish the second.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine will, bodily offering and finality.
verses.before: And by that will we have been made holy through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
verses.after: By that will we have been made holy through the offering of Jesus Christ's body once for all.
verses.tsw_comparator: And by that will we have been made holy through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

verses.rationale: Preserves standing, repetition and inability.
verses.before: And every priest stands day after day serving and offering repeatedly the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
verses.after: Every priest stands day after day performing service and offering the same sacrifices again and again, which can never remove sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: And every priest stands day after day serving and offering repeatedly the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.

verses.rationale: Keeps single enduring sacrifice and enthronement.
verses.before: But when Christ had offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins, he sat down at the right hand of God,
verses.after: But after Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, he sat down at God's right hand,
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Christ had offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins, he sat down at the right hand of God,

verses.rationale: Retains waiting and enemy-subjection image.
verses.before: waiting from that time onward until his enemies should be made a footstool for his feet.
verses.after: waiting from then on until his enemies are made a footstool for his feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: waiting from that time onward until his enemies should be made a footstool for his feet.

verses.rationale: Keeps completed perfection with ongoing sanctification.
verses.before: For by a single offering he has made complete for all time people who are being made holy.
verses.after: For by one offering he has perfected forever those who are being made holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: For by a single offering he has made complete for all time those who are being made holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves Spirit as scriptural witness.
verses.before: And the Holy Spirit also bears witness to us; for after saying,
verses.after: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after saying,
verses.tsw_comparator: And the Holy Spirit also bears witness to us; for after saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps inward law and covenant speech.

verses.after: “This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws on their hearts and write them on their minds,”
verses.tsw_comparator: “This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their hearts, and I will write them on their minds,”

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic nonremembrance.
verses.before: then he adds, “I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more.”
verses.after: he adds, “I will never again remember their sins and lawless acts.”
verses.tsw_comparator: then he adds, “I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more.”

verses.rationale: Keeps logical conclusion and cessation.
verses.before: Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer any offering for sin.
verses.after: Now where these are forgiven, there is no longer an offering for sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer any offering for sin.

verses.rationale: Retains bold access and violent means.
verses.before: So, sisters and brothers and sisters, since we have confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus,
verses.after: Therefore, brothers and sisters, since we have confidence to enter the holy place by Jesus' blood,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, sisters and brothers, since we have confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus,

verses.rationale: Keeps way, curtain and bodily interpretation.
verses.before: by the new and living way that he opened for us through the curtain—that is, through his flesh—
verses.after: by the new and living way he opened for us through the curtain—that is, through his flesh—
verses.tsw_comparator: by the new and living way that he opened for us through the curtain—that is, through his flesh—

verses.rationale: Retains priestly oversight and house.
verses.before: and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
verses.after: and since we have a great priest over God's house,
verses.tsw_comparator: and since we have a great priest over the house of God,

verses.rationale: Preserves inner/outer cleansing and confidence.
verses.before: let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of trust, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
verses.after: let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
verses.tsw_comparator: let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of trust, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

verses.rationale: Keeps perseverance grounded in divine faithfulness.
verses.before: Let us hold firmly the confession of our hope without wavering, for the one who promised is trustworthy.
verses.after: Let us hold firmly to the confession of our hope without wavering, for the one who promised is faithful.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for the one who promised is trustworthy.

verses.rationale: Retains strong provocation term directed toward good.
verses.before: And let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,
verses.after: And let us consider one another so as to provoke love and good works,
verses.tsw_comparator: And let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,

verses.rationale: Keeps communal assembly, mutual encouragement and named Day.
verses.before: not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.
verses.after: not abandoning our gathering together, as some habitually do, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
verses.tsw_comparator: not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.

verses.rationale: Preserves willful ongoing sin and severe consequence.
verses.before: For if we go on sinning deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,
verses.after: For if we deliberately continue sinning after receiving knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins remains,
verses.tsw_comparator: For if we go on sinning deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,

verses.rationale: Keeps fear, fire and consuming violence.
verses.before: but a fearful expectation of judgment and a fury of fire that will consume the adversaries.
verses.after: but only a terrifying expectation of judgment and a fury of fire that will consume God's enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: but a fearful expectation of judgment and a fury of fire that will consume the adversaries.

verses.rationale: Retains named Moses, execution and exact evidentiary number.
verses.before: Anyone who has set aside the law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
verses.after: Anyone who rejected Moses' law died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anyone who has set aside the law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

verses.rationale: Keeps three offenses, blood and rhetorical escalation.
verses.before: How much worse punishment do you think will be deserved by the one who has trampled underfoot the Son of God, and has treated as common the blood of the covenant by which they were made holy, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
verses.after: How much worse punishment do you think will be deserved by someone who trampled God's Son, treated as common the covenant blood by which that person was made holy and insulted the Spirit of grace?
verses.tsw_comparator: How much worse punishment do you think will be deserved by the one who has trampled underfoot the Son of God, and has treated as common the blood of the covenant by which they were made holy, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?

verses.rationale: Retains divine vengeance rather than authorizing personal retaliation.
verses.before: For we know the one who said, “Vengeance is mine; I will repay.” And again, “The Lord will judge his people.”
verses.after: For we know the one who said, “Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge his people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For we know the one who said, “Vengeance is mine; I will repay.” And again, “The Lord will judge his people.”

verses.rationale: Keeps stark fear and bodily fall image.
verses.before: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
verses.after: It is terrifying to fall into the hands of the living God.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

verses.rationale: Retains communal memory and athletic contest.
verses.before: But remember the former days, when after you were enlightened you endured a hard struggle with sufferings—
verses.after: But remember the earlier days when, after being enlightened, you endured a great struggle with sufferings.
verses.tsw_comparator: But remember the former days, when after you were enlightened you endured a hard struggle with sufferings—

verses.rationale: Keeps spectacle language and solidarity.
verses.before: sometimes being publicly exposed to insults and afflictions, and sometimes being partners with people who were so treated.
verses.after: At times you were publicly exposed to insults and afflictions; at other times you became partners with those treated that way.
verses.tsw_comparator: sometimes being publicly exposed to insults and afflictions, and sometimes being partners with those who were so treated.

verses.rationale: Preserves imprisonment, state/social confiscation and possession wordplay.
verses.before: For you had compassion on those in prison, and you accepted with joy the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you yourselves have a better and lasting possession.
verses.after: For you sympathized with prisoners and accepted the seizure of your possessions with joy, knowing that you yourselves had a better and lasting possession.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you had compassion on those in prison, and you accepted with joy the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you yourselves have a better and lasting possession.

verses.rationale: Keeps discard image and recompense.
verses.before: So do not throw away your confidence, which has a great reward.
verses.after: So do not throw away your confidence, which carries a great reward.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore do not throw away your confidence, which has a great reward.

verses.rationale: Retains needed perseverance and sequence.
verses.before: For you have need of endurance, so that when you have done the will of God you may receive what was promised.
verses.after: For you need endurance, so that after doing God's will you may receive the promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have need of endurance, so that when you have done the will of God you may receive what was promised.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic short time and arrival.
verses.before: “For yet a very little while, and the one who is coming will come and will not delay;
verses.after: For “in just a very little while, the coming one will come and will not delay;
verses.tsw_comparator: “For yet a very little while, and the one who is coming will come and will not delay;

verses.rationale: Follows pinned pronoun and retains divine displeasure.
verses.before: but my righteous one will live by trust, and if they shrink back, my soul takes no pleasure in them.”
verses.after: but my righteous one will live by faith, and if he draws back, my soul takes no pleasure in him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: but my righteous one will live by trust, and if they shrink back, my soul takes no pleasure in them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps group contrast and preservation.
verses.before: But we are not among people who shrink back to destruction, but among people who have trust to the preserving of the soul.
verses.after: But we do not belong to those who draw back and are destroyed, but to those who have faith and preserve their lives.
verses.tsw_comparator: But we are not among those who shrink back to destruction, but among those who have trust to the preserving of the soul.

verses.rationale: Retains substantial assurance and evidentiary conviction without reducing faith to optimism.
verses.before: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
verses.after: Now faith is the assurance of what is hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.

verses.rationale: Keeps ancestral leaders and divine testimony.
verses.before: For by it the people of old received their commendation.
verses.after: For by faith the elders received approval.
verses.tsw_comparator: For by it the people of old received their commendation.

verses.rationale: Preserves creation by speech and visible/invisible contrast.
verses.before: By faith we understand that the ages were prepared by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible.
verses.after: By faith we understand that the ages were formed by God's word, so that what is seen did not come from visible things.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith we understand that the ages were prepared by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of things that are visible.

verses.rationale: Keeps both names, comparative offering and postmortem voice.
verses.before: By faith Abel offered to God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain. Through it he received commendation as righteous, God himself bearing witness by accepting his gifts; and through his faith he still speaks, though he is dead.
verses.after: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. Through it he was approved as righteous, God testifying about his gifts; and through faith, though dead, he still speaks.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Abel offered to God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain. Through it he received commendation as righteous, God himself bearing witness by accepting his gifts; and through his faith he still speaks, though he is dead.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated translation/taking language and divine pleasure.
verses.before: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he should not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him. For before he was taken he received commendation as one who had pleased God.
verses.after: By faith Enoch was taken away so that he did not see death, and he could not be found because God had taken him. Before he was taken, he was approved as pleasing to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he should not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him. For before he was taken he received commendation as one who had pleased God.

verses.rationale: Keeps necessity, divine existence and reward.
verses.before: And without faith it is impossible to please him, for whoever would approach to God must believe that he is, and that he rewards people who seek him.
verses.after: Without faith it is impossible to please God, for anyone who approaches him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And without faith it is impossible to please him, for whoever would draw near to God must believe that he is, and that he rewards those who seek him.

verses.rationale: Preserves warning, household rescue, world judgment and inheritance.
verses.before: By faith Noah, having been warned by God about events as yet unseen, in reverent fear constructed an ark for the saving of his household. Through this faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by trust.
verses.after: By faith Noah, warned about things not yet seen, responded with reverence and built an ark to save his household. By this he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes through faith.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Noah, having been warned by God about events as yet unseen, in reverent fear constructed an ark for the saving of his household. Through this faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.

verses.rationale: Keeps call, obedience, inheritance and ignorance.
verses.before: By faith Abraham, when called, obeyed and went out to a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.
verses.after: By faith Abraham obeyed when called to leave for a place he was to receive as an inheritance. He left without knowing where he was going.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Abraham, when called, obeyed and went out to a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going.

verses.rationale: Preserves alien residence, tents and named coheirs.
verses.before: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a foreign country, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise.
verses.after: By faith he lived as a foreigner in the promised land as in a land belonging to others, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of the same promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a foreign country, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise.

verses.rationale: Keeps city, foundations and two divine craft roles.
verses.before: For he was looking forward to the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
verses.after: For he was waiting for the city with foundations, whose designer and builder is God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he was looking forward to the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned Sarah-as-subject reading and retains bodily impossibility.
verses.before: By faith Sarah herself, though barren, received power to conceive seed, even when she was past the proper age, since she considered him faithful who had promised.
verses.after: By faith Sarah herself received power to conceive, even past the proper age, because she considered the one who promised faithful.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Sarah herself, though barren, received power to conceive seed, even when she was past the proper age, since she considered him faithful who had promised.

verses.rationale: Keeps near-death, both vast-number similes and descent.
verses.before: So from one man, and him as good as dead, were born descendants as many as the stars of heaven and as the innumerable grains of sand by the seashore.
verses.after: Therefore, from one man—and one already as good as dead—came descendants as numerous as the stars in heaven and as countless as the sand along the seashore.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore from one man, and him as good as dead, were born descendants as many as the stars of heaven and as the innumerable grains of sand by the seashore.

verses.rationale: Preserves death before fulfillment and alien identity.
verses.before: All these died in faith, not having received what was promised, but having seen and greeted them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.
verses.after: All these died in faith without receiving the promises. They saw and welcomed them from far away and confessed that they were strangers and temporary residents on the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: All these died in faith, not having received what was promised, but having seen and greeted them from afar, and having confessed that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps inferential homeland longing.
verses.before: For people who say such things make it clear that they are seeking a homeland.
verses.after: People who speak this way make it clear that they are seeking a homeland.
verses.tsw_comparator: For people who say such things make it clear that they are seeking a homeland.

verses.rationale: Preserves counterfactual and available return.
verses.before: If they had been thinking of the land that they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.
verses.after: If they had been remembering the land they left, they would have had opportunity to return.
verses.tsw_comparator: If they had been thinking of the land that they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.

verses.rationale: Keeps better/heavenly identification and divine city preparation.
verses.before: But as it is, they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared for them a city.
verses.after: But now they desire a better land—a heavenly one. Therefore, God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as it is, they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared for them a city.

verses.rationale: Retains the attempted child sacrifice, both names and promise tension.
verses.before: By faith Abraham, when he was being tested, offered up Isaac, and the one who had received the promises was offering up his only son,
verses.after: By faith Abraham, when tested, offered Isaac. The one who had received the promises was offering his one and only son,
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Abraham, when he was being tested, offered up Isaac, and the one who had received the promises was offering up his only son,

verses.rationale: Keeps named son and lineage quotation.
verses.before: of whom it was said, “Through Isaac will your descendants be called.”
verses.after: about whom it had been said, “Through Isaac your offspring will be named.”
verses.tsw_comparator: of whom it was said, “Through Isaac shall your descendants be called.”

verses.rationale: Preserves resurrection reasoning and parable-like return.
verses.before: He reasoned that God was able even to raise him from the dead—and figuratively he did receive him back.
verses.after: Abraham reasoned that God was able even to raise someone from the dead, and in a figurative sense he did receive Isaac back.
verses.tsw_comparator: He reasoned that God was able even to raise him from the dead—and figuratively he did receive him back.

verses.rationale: Keeps all names and future orientation.
verses.before: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, concerning what was to come.
verses.after: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau regarding things to come.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, concerning what was to come.

verses.rationale: Retains death setting, both grandsons collectively and staff.
verses.before: By faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and bowed in worship over the head of his staff.
verses.after: By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons and worshiped while leaning on the top of his staff.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and bowed in worship over the head of his staff.

verses.rationale: Keeps exodus anticipation and burial remains.
verses.before: By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus of the Israelites and gave directions concerning his bones.
verses.after: By faith Joseph, near the end of his life, mentioned the exodus of Israel's children and gave instructions about his bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, made mention of the exodus of the Israelites and gave directions concerning his bones.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact duration, both parents and royal threat.
verses.before: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the king’s edict.
verses.after: By faith Moses, after he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the king's decree.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the king’s edict.

verses.rationale: Keeps identity refusal and named royal relation.
verses.before: By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,
verses.after: By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called a son of Pharaoh's daughter.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter,

verses.rationale: Retains chosen affliction and brief pleasure.
verses.before: choosing rather to suffer ill-treatment with the people of God than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin.
verses.after: He chose to suffer mistreatment with God's people rather than enjoy sin's temporary pleasure.
verses.tsw_comparator: choosing rather to suffer ill-treatment with the people of God than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin.

verses.rationale: Keeps surprising Christ reference and economic comparison.
verses.before: He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward.
verses.after: He considered disgrace for the Christ greater wealth than Egypt's treasures, because he was looking toward the reward.
verses.tsw_comparator: He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to the reward.

verses.rationale: Preserves departure, royal rage and paradoxical sight.
verses.before: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the anger of the king; for he endured as seeing him who is invisible.
verses.after: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the king's anger, for he persevered as though seeing the invisible one.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the anger of the king; for he endured as seeing him who is invisible.

verses.rationale: Keeps named feast, blood and lethal threat.
verses.before: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn might not touch them.
verses.after: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn might not touch them.

verses.rationale: Retains named sea, miracle and drowning.
verses.before: By faith the people crossed the Red Sea as on dry land; but the Egyptians, when they attempted to do the same, were swallowed up.
verses.after: By faith they crossed the Red Sea as on dry land; when the Egyptians attempted it, they were swallowed up.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith the people crossed the Red Sea as on dry land; but the Egyptians, when they attempted to do the same, were swallowed up.

verses.rationale: Keeps place, walls and exact duration.
verses.before: By faith the walls of Jericho fell after they had been encircled for seven days.
verses.after: By faith Jericho's walls fell after being encircled for seven days.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith the walls of Jericho fell after they had been encircled for seven days.

verses.rationale: Keeps name, stigmatized occupation and protective reception.
verses.before: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with people who were disobedient, because she had received the spies in peace.
verses.after: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who disobeyed, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who were disobedient, because she had received the spies in peace.

verses.rationale: Preserves all six names and rhetorical compression.
verses.before: And what more will I say? For time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets,
verses.after: And what more should I say? Time would fail me if I told about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: And what more shall I say? For time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets,

verses.rationale: Keeps military, ethical, promissory and animal actions.
verses.before: who through trust conquered kingdoms, did what was right, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
verses.after: Through faith they conquered kingdoms, practiced justice, obtained promises and shut lions' mouths.
verses.tsw_comparator: who through faith conquered kingdoms, did what was right, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,

verses.rationale: Retains fire, lethal weapon, reversal and battle violence.
verses.before: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, put foreign armies to flight.
verses.after: They quenched raging fire, escaped the edge of the sword, gained strength from weakness, became mighty in war and put foreign armies to flight.
verses.tsw_comparator: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, put foreign armies to flight.

verses.rationale: Keeps women as agents/recipients, torture and chosen nonrelease.
verses.before: Women received back their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, refusing release, so that they might rise to a better life.
verses.after: Women received their dead back by resurrection. Others were tortured, refusing release so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
verses.tsw_comparator: Women received back their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured, refusing release, so that they might rise to a better life.

verses.rationale: Preserves all public and custodial abuse.
verses.before: Still others suffered mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
verses.after: Others experienced mockery and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Still others suffered mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.

verses.rationale: Keeps graphic killings, clothing and three forms of deprivation.
verses.before: They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were killed by the sword. They went about in skins of sheep and goats, destitute, afflicted, mistreated—
verses.after: They were stoned, sawn in two and killed by the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted and mistreated—
verses.tsw_comparator: They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were killed by the sword. They went about in skins of sheep and goats, destitute, afflicted, mistreated—

verses.rationale: Retains evaluative reversal and every refuge.
verses.before: of whom the world was not worthy—wandering over deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the ground.
verses.after: the world was not worthy of them—wandering in deserts, mountains, caves and holes in the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: of whom the world was not worthy—wandering over deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps testimony and delayed fulfillment.
verses.before: And all these, though commended for their trust, did not receive what was promised,
verses.after: All these were approved through their faith, yet they did not receive the promise,
verses.tsw_comparator: And all these, though commended for their faith, did not receive what was promised,

verses.rationale: Preserves intergenerational completion and inclusion.
verses.before: since God had provided something better for us, that apart from us they should not be made complete.
verses.after: because God had provided something better for us, so that they would not be perfected without us.
verses.tsw_comparator: since God had provided something better for us, that apart from us they should not be made complete.

verses.rationale: Keeps crowd, encumbrance and race imagery.
verses.before: So, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight and sin that clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race set before us,
verses.after: Therefore, since we too are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight and the sin that so easily entangles us, and run with endurance the race set before us,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight and sin that clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race set before us,

verses.rationale: Preserves cross as shameful execution, joy and enthronement.
verses.before: looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of faith, who for the joy set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
verses.after: fixing our eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of faith. For the joy set before him, he endured a cross, despising its shame, and sat down at the right hand of God's throne.
verses.tsw_comparator: looking to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of faith, who for the joy set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps hostile contradiction and inner exhaustion.
verses.before: Consider him who endured from sinners such hostility against himself, so that you may not grow weary or fainthearted.
verses.after: Consider the one who endured such hostility from sinners against himself, so that you do not grow weary and lose heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Consider him who endured from sinners such hostility against himself, so that you may not grow weary or fainthearted.

verses.rationale: Retains combat image and lethal limit.
verses.before: In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.
verses.after: In struggling against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.

verses.rationale: Keeps masculine filial quotation and correction.
verses.before: And have you forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons? “My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor be weary when reproved by him.
verses.after: And you have forgotten the encouragement that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not make light of the Lord's discipline or give up when he corrects you,
verses.tsw_comparator: And have you forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons? “My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor be weary when reproved by him.

verses.rationale: Retains corporal violence in the source's parental analogy.
verses.before: For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and chastises every son whom he receives.”
verses.after: for the Lord disciplines the one he loves and flogs every son he receives.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and chastises every son whom he receives.”

verses.rationale: Keeps gendered family argument and endurance.
verses.before: It is for discipline that you have to endure. God is treating you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline?
verses.after: Endure for discipline. God is treating you as sons, for what son is not disciplined by his father?
verses.tsw_comparator: It is for discipline that you have to endure. God is treating you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline?

verses.rationale: Preserves stigmatizing legitimacy language rather than sanitizing it.
verses.before: If you are left without discipline, in which all have participated, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
verses.after: But if you are without discipline, in which all sons share, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you are left without discipline, in which all have participated, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.

verses.rationale: Keeps father comparison, submission and life.
verses.before: Besides this, we have had earthly fathers who disciplined us and we respected them. Will we not much more be subject to the Father of spirits and live?
verses.after: Furthermore, we had human fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Should we not much more submit to the Father of spirits and live?
verses.tsw_comparator: Besides this, we have had earthly fathers who disciplined us and we respected them. Shall we not much more be subject to the Father of spirits and live?

verses.rationale: Retains human fallibility contrast and intended participation.
verses.before: For they disciplined us for a short time as it seemed best to them, but he disciplines us for our good, that we may share his holiness.
verses.after: They disciplined us for a short time as seemed best to them, but God disciplines us for our benefit, so that we may share his holiness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they disciplined us for a short time as it seemed best to them, but he disciplines us for our good, that we may share his holiness.

verses.rationale: Keeps pain, training and fruit.
verses.before: For the moment all discipline seems painful rather than pleasant, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to people who have been trained by it.
verses.after: No discipline seems joyful at the time, but painful. Later, however, it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained by it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the moment all discipline seems painful rather than pleasant, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily exhaustion and restoration.
verses.before: So lift your drooping hands and strengthen your weak knees,
verses.after: Therefore, strengthen drooping hands and weakened knees,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore lift your drooping hands and strengthen your weak knees,

verses.rationale: Keeps path, disability and healing imagery.
verses.before: and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame may not be put out of joint but instead be healed.
verses.after: and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame may not be dislocated but healed instead.
verses.tsw_comparator: and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame may not be put out of joint but rather be healed.

verses.rationale: Retains universal peace and necessary holiness.
verses.before: Strive for peace with everyone, and for the holiness without which no one will see the Lord.
verses.after: Pursue peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Strive for peace with everyone, and for the holiness without which no one will see the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps communal oversight, root and spreading contamination.
verses.before: See to it that no one fails to obtain the grace of God; that no root of bitterness springs up and causes trouble, and by it many become defiled;
verses.after: Watch carefully that no one falls short of God's grace and that no root of bitterness grows up to cause trouble and defile many.
verses.tsw_comparator: See to it that no one fails to obtain the grace of God; that no root of bitterness springs up and causes trouble, and by it many become defiled;

verses.rationale: Preserves named example, birthright and exact price.
verses.before: that no one is sexually immoral or unholy like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.
verses.after: See that no one is sexually immoral or profane like Esau, who sold his own birthright for one meal.
verses.tsw_comparator: that no one is sexually immoral or unholy like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.

verses.rationale: Keeps rejection, ambiguous repentance/change and grief.
verses.before: For you know that afterward, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no chance to repent, though he sought it with tears.
verses.after: For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. He found no opportunity for a change of mind, though he sought the blessing with tears.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you know that afterward, when he desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no chance to repent, though he sought it with tears.

verses.rationale: Retains tangible mountain and four terrifying phenomena.
verses.before: For you have not come to what may be touched, a blazing fire and darkness and gloom and a tempest
verses.after: For you have not come to something that can be touched, to blazing fire, darkness, gloom and storm,
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have not come to what may be touched, a blazing fire and darkness and gloom and a tempest

verses.rationale: Keeps sound and fearful refusal.
verses.before: and the sound of a trumpet and a voice whose words made the hearers beg that no further messages be spoken to them.
verses.after: to a trumpet blast and a voice whose words made the hearers beg that no further message be spoken to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the sound of a trumpet and a voice whose words made the hearers beg that no further messages be spoken to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves animal death and mountain boundary.
verses.before: For they could not endure the order that was given, “If even a beast touches the mountain, it will be stoned.”
verses.after: For they could not bear the command, “Even if an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For they could not endure the order that was given, “If even a beast touches the mountain, it shall be stoned.”

verses.rationale: Keeps named Moses and doubled fear.
verses.before: Indeed, so terrifying was the sight that Moses said, “I tremble with fear.”
verses.after: The sight was so terrifying that Moses said, “I am terrified and trembling.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, so terrifying was the sight that Moses said, “I tremble with fear.”

verses.rationale: Retains all place names, innumerable angels and festal gathering.
verses.before: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering,
verses.after: But you have come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and tens of thousands of angels in joyful assembly,
verses.tsw_comparator: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering,

verses.rationale: Keeps heavenly registry, universal judge and perfected spirits.
verses.before: and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God, the judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
verses.after: to the assembly of the firstborn enrolled in heaven, to God the judge of all and to the spirits of righteous people made perfect,
verses.tsw_comparator: and to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God, the judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,

verses.rationale: Preserves mediator, ritual blood and named comparison.
verses.before: and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
verses.after: to Jesus, mediator of a new covenant, and to sprinkled blood that speaks better than Abel's blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.

verses.rationale: Keeps earth/heaven escalation and communal warning.
verses.before: See that you do not refuse him who is speaking. For if they did not escape when they refused him who warned them on earth, much less will we escape if we reject him who warns from heaven.
verses.after: See that you do not refuse the one who speaks. If they did not escape when they refused the one who warned them on earth, how much less will we if we turn away from the one who warns from heaven?
verses.tsw_comparator: See that you do not refuse him who is speaking. For if they did not escape when they refused him who warned them on earth, much less will we escape if we reject him who warns from heaven.

verses.rationale: Retains past quake, future promise and cosmic scope.
verses.before: At that time his voice shook the earth, but now he has promised, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heavens.”
verses.after: At that time his voice shook the earth, but now he has promised, “Once more I will shake not only the earth but also heaven.”
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time his voice shook the earth, but now he has promised, “Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heavens.”

verses.rationale: Keeps interpretive conclusion and creation's removal.
verses.before: This phrase, “Yet once more,” indicates the removal of things that are shaken—that is, things that have been made—so that the things that cannot be shaken may remain.
verses.after: The words “once more” indicate the removal of what can be shaken—that is, created things—so that what cannot be shaken may remain.
verses.tsw_comparator: This phrase, “Yet once more,” indicates the removal of things that are shaken—that is, things that have been made—in order that the things that cannot be shaken may remain.

verses.rationale: Preserves kingdom, gratitude and fearful worship.
verses.before: So let us be grateful for receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, and thus let us offer to God acceptable worship, with reverence and awe,
verses.after: Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us be grateful and in this way worship God acceptably with reverence and awe,
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore let us be grateful for receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, and thus let us offer to God acceptable worship, with reverence and awe,

verses.rationale: Keeps the stark fire image.
verses.before: for our God is a consuming fire.
verses.after: for our God is a consuming fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: for our God is a consuming fire.

verses.rationale: Retains sibling-love term and ongoing command.
verses.before: Let brotherly love continue.
verses.after: Let family love continue.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let brotherly love continue.

verses.rationale: Keeps stranger-love and hidden angelic visitors.
verses.before: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels without knowing it.
verses.after: Do not neglect hospitality, for through it some have welcomed angels without knowing it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels without knowing it.

verses.rationale: Preserves embodied solidarity with incarceration and abuse.
verses.before: Remember people who are in prison, as if in prison with them, and people who are mistreated, since you also are in the body.
verses.after: Remember those in prison as though imprisoned with them, and those being mistreated as people who are yourselves in a body.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them, and those who are mistreated, since you also are in the body.

verses.rationale: Keeps public honor, sexual integrity and judgment.
verses.before: Let marriage be held in honor among all, and let the marriage bed be undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterous.
verses.after: Let marriage be honored by everyone and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let marriage be held in honor among all, and let the marriage bed be undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterous.

verses.rationale: Preserves economic warning and emphatic promise.
verses.before: Keep your life free from love of money, and be content with what you have, for he has said, “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”
verses.after: Keep your life free from love of money, and be content with what you have, for he has said, “I will never leave you and never abandon you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Keep your life free from love of money, and be content with what you have, for he has said, “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps courage, divine aid and rhetorical question.
verses.before: So we can confidently say, “The Lord is my helper; I will not fear; what can man do to me?”
verses.after: So we may say with confidence, “The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can a human being do to me?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So we can confidently say, “The Lord is my helper; I will not fear; what can man do to me?”

verses.rationale: Retains former leaders, life outcome and imitation.
verses.before: Remember your leaders, people who spoke to you the word of God. Consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their trust.
verses.after: Remember your leaders who spoke God's word to you. Consider the outcome of their way of life and imitate their faith.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember your leaders, those who spoke to you the word of God. Consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.

verses.rationale: Preserves threefold temporal constancy.
verses.before: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
verses.after: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.

verses.rationale: Keeps movement image, heart and ineffective food regulations.
verses.before: Do not be led away by diverse and strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods, which have not benefited those devoted to them.
verses.after: Do not be carried away by various strange teachings. It is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods that have not benefited those who follow such practices.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be led away by diverse and strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods, which have not benefited those devoted to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves cultic exclusion and right.
verses.before: We have an altar from which people who serve the tent have no right to eat.
verses.after: We have an altar from which those who serve at the tent have no right to eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: We have an altar from which those who serve the tent have no right to eat.

verses.rationale: Keeps animal bodies, blood and spatial exclusion.
verses.before: For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the holy places by the high priest as a sacrifice for sin are burned outside the camp.
verses.after: The bodies of the animals whose blood is brought into the holy place by the high priest as an offering for sin are burned outside the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the holy places by the high priest as a sacrifice for sin are burned outside the camp.

verses.rationale: Retains execution suffering, location and blood.
verses.before: So Jesus also suffered outside the gate in order to sanctify the people through his own blood.
verses.after: Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate in order to make the people holy through his own blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jesus also suffered outside the gate in order to sanctify the people through his own blood.

verses.rationale: Keeps spatial solidarity and shame.
verses.before: So let us go to him outside the camp and bear the reproach he endured.
verses.after: So let us go out to him outside the camp, bearing his disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore let us go to him outside the camp and bear the reproach he endured.

verses.rationale: Preserves unsettled present and future city.
verses.before: For here we have no lasting city, but we seek the city that is to come.
verses.after: For here we have no lasting city, but we seek the one to come.
verses.tsw_comparator: For here we have no lasting city, but we seek the city that is to come.

verses.rationale: Keeps sacrificial metaphor and lip-fruit explanation.
verses.before: Through him then let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that acknowledge his name.
verses.after: Through Jesus, then, let us continually offer God a sacrifice of praise—the fruit of lips that confess his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: Through him then let us continually offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that acknowledge his name.

verses.rationale: Retains practical sacrifices and divine pleasure.
verses.before: Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.
verses.after: Do not neglect doing good and sharing, for God is pleased with such sacrifices.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.

verses.rationale: Keeps authority, leaders' accountability and community effect.
verses.before: Obey your leaders and give way to them, for they are watch over your souls as people who will give an account. Let them do this with joy and not with sighing, for that would be harmful to you.
verses.after: Obey your leaders and yield to them, for they keep watch over your lives as those who will give an account. Let them do this with joy and not groaning, for that would be unprofitable for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Obey your leaders and give way to them, for they are watch over your souls as those who will give an account. Let them do this with joy and not with sighing, for that would be harmful to you.

verses.rationale: Retains prayer request, conscience and intention.
verses.before: Pray for us, for we are sure that we have a clear conscience, desiring to act honorably in everything.
verses.after: Pray for us, for we are convinced that we have a good conscience and desire to conduct ourselves honorably in everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pray for us, for we are sure that we have a clear conscience, desiring to act honorably in all things.

verses.rationale: Keeps intensified request and hoped return.
verses.before: I urge you the more earnestly to do this so that I may be restored to you sooner.
verses.after: I urge you all the more to do this, so that I may be restored to you soon.
verses.tsw_comparator: I urge you the more earnestly to do this in order that I may be restored to you sooner.

verses.rationale: Preserves resurrection, shepherd image and covenant blood.
verses.before: Now may the God of peace, who brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant,
verses.after: Now may the God of peace, who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant,
verses.tsw_comparator: Now may the God of peace, who brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant,

verses.rationale: Keeps divine equipping, inward work and doxology.
verses.before: equip you with everything good that you may do his will, working in us what is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
verses.after: equip you with every good thing to do his will, working in us what is pleasing before him through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever. Amen.
verses.tsw_comparator: equip you with everything good that you may do his will, working in us that which is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

verses.rationale: Preserves authorial appeal and ironic brevity claim.
verses.before: I appeal to you, brothers and sisters, bear with my word of exhortation, for I have written to you briefly.
verses.after: I urge you, brothers and sisters, to bear with this word of encouragement, for I have written to you briefly.
verses.tsw_comparator: I appeal to you, brothers, bear with my word of exhortation, for I have written to you briefly.

verses.rationale: Keeps named Timothy, release and conditional visit.
verses.before: You should know that our brother Timothy has been released, with whom I will see you if he comes soon.
verses.after: You should know that our brother Timothy has been released. If he comes soon, I will see you with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: You should know that our brother Timothy has been released, with whom I shall see you if he comes soon.

verses.rationale: Retains both recipient groups and geographic origin.
verses.before: Greet all your leaders and all the saints. People who come from Italy send you greetings.
verses.after: Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy greet you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those who come from Italy send you greetings.

verses.rationale: Preserves inclusive short blessing.
verses.before: Grace be with all of you.
verses.after: Grace be with all of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Grace be with all of you.
